hints: Focus on the type of structure and bonding in each compound, giant versus simple molecular makes all the difference to melting point.
Remember that $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent lattice with very strong bonds, while $\text{SiCl}_4$ is a simple covalent molecule held by weak van der Waals forces.
Think about hydrolysis: covalent chlorides like $\text{SiCl}_4$ react vigorously with water to give acidic fumes, while ionic $\text{NaCl}$ just dissolves.
walkthrough:
**Check Statement 1: $\text{SiCl}_4$ vs $\text{SiO}_2$**

Think structure first. $\text{SiO}_2$ has a giant covalent network of strong Si-O bonds in all directions.

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is a simple molecular liquid with only weak instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces between molecules. So $\text{SiO}_2$ melts at about 1600 C, $\text{SiCl}_4$ melts at about -70 C. Statement 1 is false.

**Check Statement 2: Reaction with water**

Covalent chlorides of Period 3 hydrolyse in water. Ionic chlorides just dissolve.

$$\text{SiCl}_4(l) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2(s) + 4\text{HCl}(g)$$

$\text{NaCl}$ dissolves to give hydrated ions but does not react to form $\text{HCl}$. So statement 2 is true.

**Check Statement 3: $\text{SiCl}_4$ vs $\text{NaCl}$**

$\text{NaCl}$ is a giant ionic lattice with strong electrostatic attraction between $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions, melting at 801 C.

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is simple molecular with weak intermolecular forces, so its melting point is far lower. So statement 3 is true.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statement 1 is false, statements 2 and 3 are true.

That combination corresponds to 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong because giant covalent $\text{SiO}_2$ has a much higher melting point than simple molecular $\text{SiCl}_4$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Although statement 2 is correct, statement 1 is false for the same giant versus simple molecular reason.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is true because $\text{SiCl}_4$ hydrolyses to $\text{SiO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ while $\text{NaCl}$ only dissolves. Statement 3 is true because giant ionic $\text{NaCl}$ has a much higher melting point than simple molecular $\text{SiCl}_4$.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only statement 1 is correct. In fact statement 1 is the only false statement, while 2 and 3 are true.
